conflict_synopsis.core_view: AONIA/ASX price zero cuts through Feb-2028 and +21.5bp by October even though the RBA housing channel is already in a pandemic-sized slump, so Australian front-end hike pricing is the underpriced easing.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: ASX October/November AONIA fails to deliver the priced +21.5bp/+33.5bp as housing and labour keep deteriorating.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: AONIA-implied rates keep climbing along the +51 to +59.5bp hike path, or trimmed-mean CPI re-accelerates from 3.6%.

paper_capital.rationale: The 5% ACT/365 vig is charged on the full $100m even if flat, so remaining idle cannot beat the hurdle. Packet analog 2022-09-28 shows a 37.4bp 1m rally in AU 2Y after a similar +39bp 1m sell-off; that is the edge, not a mark. $40m is 40% of the seed, leaving room for the 2025-12 continuation analog and the inflation-82 risk. No executable broker price is in the packet, so this is paper risk appetite rather than a quoted DV01; parent may record execution_blocked.

remit: underpriced easing, lower-rate repricing, or growth weakness
stance_summary: Verified frozen SOFR/CORRA/AONIA paths price no easing anywhere in the US/CA/AU set: SOFR 3.85 with +34.75bp by Dec-2026 and +75.25bp by Aug-2028; CORRA 2.29 with +29bp on the 1m strip by Dec-2026 and +136.5bp on the 3m strip by Sep-2028; AONIA 4.35 with +21.5bp by Oct-2026, +51bp by Mar-2027 and a peak +59.5bp with still +49bp in Feb-2028. Inference: restrictive policy is already biting in Australian housing and Canadian labour, so the hike-heavy paths are the underpriced-easing discrepancy. Unknown: live broker marks, RBA meeting probabilities, and whether energy pass-through overrides the housing channel. Primary expression is outright long AU 2Y.

catalysts: October/November AONIA contracts fail to realise the priced +21.5bp/+33.5bp as RBA communication or incoming housing/labour data cap hikes.
Further NSW/national housing volume, price or stamp-duty deterioration.
Canadian-style labour confirmation that imported global hike pricing is over-fitted to energy headlines.
Softening of the energy-inflation tail (Saudi workaround already in the packet) that currently supports the desk tightening narrative.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Verified: RBA tightening is already transmitting through housing (NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% y/y in August, transaction volumes -18%, Sydney and Melbourne values down more than 7% from peak), AU employment -15.8k in July, unemployment 4.5%, and September Westpac-MI sentiment -5.2% to 84.4. Inference: a still-restrictive AONIA 4.35 plus another 50-60bp of priced hikes tightens real activity further, forcing the RBA off the hike path sooner than ASX cash futures imply. The closing mechanism is a bullish re-pricing of the 2026-10 through 2027-03 AONIA strip and a decline in AU 2Y from 4.999.
context_build.flow_and_positioning_check: CFTC TFF as of 2026-09-15: AUD futures open interest 493141, 99.0th percentile 1y / 99.7th 3y, weekly +37673, z_1y +3.61 — crowding is in AUD futures plumbing, not in identified net direction (leveraged/asset-manager net are null). US2Y OI 4.43m is only 24.0th percentile 1y; US10Y OI 41.3rd percentile 1y. CME volume overlay unavailable (HTTP 403). Paper books are empty $100m seeds with no open positions. Inference: extreme AUD OI can amplify an AUDUSD squeeze but does not explain why AONIA still prices hikes; rates expression avoids that crowded FX surface. Unknown: trader-class net for AUD and any ASX cash-futures holder split beyond listed OI/volume.

historical_reference.distribution: AU 2Y 4.999 sits at the 99.01st percentile over 1y and 99.80th over 5y (z_1y +1.67, z_5y +1.50). AU 10Y 5.348 is similarly extreme (99.01st/99.80th, z_1y +2.06). AU 2s10s 34.9bp is only 24.4th percentile 1y. AU-US 2Y +25.9bp is 25.6th percentile 1y but 84.7th percentile 5y. These percentiles are discovery context, not the thesis.
historical_reference.regime_differences: 2022-09 analog occurred at a much lower yield (3.572 vs 4.999) around a global gilt/vol shock, not an energy-inflation and housing-slump mix. 2022-01 and 2023-05 analogs were early or mid hiking cycles with inflation still accelerating; today AU headline CPI has already eased to 3.5% from 3.8% though trimmed mean remains 3.6%. Current regime adds a live energy shock, a Fed-on-hold-to-hike global term-premium impulse, BoJ tightening, and a broken live AU OIS vintage. No analog is a one-for-one match; 2022-09 is the closest post-spike rally, 2025-12 is the closest continuation risk.

independent_checks: Policy-path check: live AONIA 4.35 plus ASX 30-day cash futures (not the 01-Dec-2022 OIS prints) show zero cuts and +21.5/+51/+59.5bp of extra tightening.
Physical housing check: NSW stamp duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak — the RBA channel is already biting.
Labour/sentiment check: employment -15.8k, unemployment 4.5%, WPI +3.2% y/y versus +3.4% a year earlier, September Westpac-MI 84.4 (-5.2%).

Cross-market: CA labour already weak (employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y, CPI-trim 1.9%/median 2.0%) while 3m CORRA still prices +136.5bp of hikes — same global-hike-import pattern, supporting that domestic softness is not being allowed to reprice paths.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: global tightening after the Fed move, energy-shock inflation tail, AU trimmed-mean CPI still 3.6% y/y in July, inflation gauge 82. New/now-binding: 16 Sep housing print showing a pandemic-sized stamp-duty hole; September consumer-sentiment drop; live ASX path still adding 21.5bp by October rather than fading after the housing evidence. Known facts explain the current high AU yield level; they do not justify incremental near-term hike pricing once the housing channel is visibly broken.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that Australia can deliver +21.5bp by October and +51 to +59.5bp of extra tightening while housing volumes, prices and stamp-duty receipts are already contracting at pandemic scale and labour/sentiment are softening. The priced path is a continued hiking cycle; the dove discrepancy is that the next impulse is lower-rate repricing, not more hikes.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: Verified priced assumption from AONIA/ASX: no cuts through Feb-2028; about two additional 25bp hikes by March 2027; peak cash rate near 4.95. US SOFR prices no cuts and +75bp to Aug-2028. CA 1m CORRA prices +29bp by Dec-2026; CA 3m CORRA prices a full re-hiking cycle to 3.655 (+136.5bp) by Sep-2028. Desk-implied: energy and global term-rate pressure dominate domestic growth softness.

Desk thesis 18 Sep: energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse and keeping term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer. AU 2Y is 4.999 as of 16 Sep (99.0th percentile 1y and 5y, z_1y +1.67) with analog prior-1m move about +39bp. AONIA 4.35 as of 17 Sep; ASX 30D cash futures price 4.355 (Sep), 4.565 (Oct, +21.5bp, OI 21752, volume 4450), 4.685 (Nov, +33.5bp), 4.725 (Dec, +37.5bp), 4.86 (Mar-2027, +51bp) and peak 4.945 (+59.5bp) in Jul-Sep 2027, still 4.84 (+49bp) in Feb-2028. Bank bills 4.41/4.68/5.07 (1m/3m/6m). AU-US 2Y spread +25.9bp as of 16 Sep, -11.5bp over 1m. AUDUSD 0.712, 1m +0.20%, 5d -0.73%. Unknown: 1d/1m AU yield changes are null in the tenor block; official RBA F1 OIS is 01-Dec-2022 vintage and must not be used as live OIS.

policy_path_check.rationale: AU_2Y is a short-end AU rates trade, so the live AONIA benchmark and ASX cash-futures path are the required policy-path layer; sovereign 2Y 4.999 is not a substitute. US and CA paths are included because the desk narrative is a global hike impulse; they confirm that easing is not priced in any of the three live strips and that CA 3m CORRA in particular prices +136.5bp of extra tightening despite core inflation already near 2%.

Inference: the marginal driver of the 2Y is the still-rising AONIA path imported from the global tightening/energy narrative, not a domestic demand boom (activity 54, consumer 48, labour 50).

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Outright long AU 2Y government duration (receive Australian 2-year yields), with the same view alternatively expressed as long ASX 30-day AONIA cash-rate futures concentrated in the 2026-10/2026-11 contracts where implied rates are 4.565 and 4.685 versus AONIA 4.35.

Spot AUDUSD mixes China/copper/risk and CFTC AUD open interest is already at the 99.0th percentile 1y, so FX is a noisier, more crowded owner of the same macro. trade.invalidation: Thesis invalid if ASX AONIA-implied rates keep rising along the priced +51bp (Mar-2027) to +59.5bp (mid-2027) hike path without offsetting housing/labour deterioration, or if AU trimmed-mean CPI re-accelerates from the July 3.6% y/y print.
trade.mispricing: ASX AONIA prices a continued hiking cycle (no cuts, +21.5bp by Oct, +51bp by Mar-2027) as if the housing channel had not already produced a pandemic-sized revenue and price hole. That is overpriced tightening / underpriced easing in the Australian front end. AU 2Y 4.999 embeds that path plus term premium; a 2022-09-28-style 1m rally of 37.4bp is one packet analog, not a target.

trade.structure: Outright long Australian 2-year government duration (receive AU 2Y). Alternate implementation: long ASX 30-day AONIA 2026-10 and 2026-11 cash-rate futures. Research/reference only; no executable broker structure in the packet.
trade.thesis: FACT: AONIA 4.35 and the ASX 30-day strip price zero cuts through Feb-2028 and +21.5bp of hikes by October, +51bp by March 2027 and a peak +59.5bp, while NSW housing transactions and stamp duty have already collapsed and AU labour/sentiment are softening. FACT: AU 2Y 4.999 is at the 99th percentile 1y and 5y. INFERENCE: restrictive policy is biting through the housing channel faster than hawks and the global-tightening desk narrative admit, so the next AU front-end impulse is lower-rate repricing rather than delivery of the priced hikes. INFERENCE: receiving AU 2Y owns that path discrepancy more cleanly than short AUDUSD. UNKNOWN: executable entry, RBA meeting dates/odds, and whether 3.6% trimmed-mean inflation plus the energy shock keep the RBA hiking into the slump.
why_now: 16 Sep housing evidence is now in the frozen packet while the 18 Sep desk thesis still treats global tightening as dominant even where domestic growth is softer.
ASX October AONIA already implies 4.565 versus 4.35 with 4450 contracts of volume and 21752 open interest — the near-term hike is live, not a distant terminal debate.
September Westpac-MI sentiment fell 5.2% to 84.4, a fresh demand-side impulse after July employment -15.8k.
Seat is flat on a $100m book that pays 5% ACT/365 regardless; remaining idle does not stop the vig and the packet now shows a defined AU path discrepancy.
